message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large—on the order of **10⁴³**.  

This figure comes from combinatorial estimates that count all ways the 32 pieces can be arranged on the 64 squares while respecting the rules (e.g., no two kings in check, pawns only on ranks 2–7, etc.). It’s often cited as “the Shannon number” for position space, and it gives a sense of how vast the search space is for computer engines.
